clauses.reason: Executive Order 10933, signed 1961-04-12, extends the time within which Emergency Board No. 136, created by Executive Order 10923, must report to the President. It says that board is "authorized to make its report to the" President "on any day prior to May 24," 1961, and that the thirty-day period after the report under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act "included in the extension of time" provided by the order. The dossier’s clause span began mid-sentence at the words "1961. The thirty-day period" and left out the authorizing sentence, so I replaced it with the complete operative text, from "By virtue of the authority" through "provided by this Order." (offsets 827-1362 of the held text). The extension is a report deadline and not an end. The held NMB report text for Emergency Board No. 136 (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10933_Actual_date_of_the_Emergency_Board_No._136_Northwest_Airlines_Inc._created_by_EO_1092_f900c4013d.txt) gives the date May 24, 1961 on its cover and letter of transmittal, the same day as the authorized-before date in this order; a dated letter is not proof of when the President received the report, and the thirty-day period after that date would have run through 1961-06-23. The order was functionally spent by then if the board reported on that date (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded); that is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16007: the number 10933 followed by the subject Extending an emergency board to investigate airline labor disputes, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 also lists EO 10923, the order this one amends. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
EO 10933 extends the report time of the Northwest Airlines emergency board created by EO 10923; provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text and found that the dossier’s single clause omitted the authorizing sentence, so I corrected the inventory to the complete operative paragraph. The extension is a report deadline, not an end. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) revokes it by number. The machine searches carry no coverage warning and show no contrary hit; the dossier’s name-match lead EO 11028 (a national-forest transfer order) is unrelated and cites no change to this order.

The corrected inventory is a single clause containing the whole operative paragraph."}

savings.reason: EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language: a search of the whole held text for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving, pending and similar words found only incidental uses inside other orders’ subject lines. The extension had no continuing effect after the board’s report time passed; the board’s report and any later settlement rest on the Railway Labor Act and the parties’ acts.
